summary:
Our interactive 2D space mission simulator transforms complex aerospace engineering into an exciting adventure for young learners. Players design spacecraft by balancing real-world trade-offs like budget, mass, power, and fuel. While exploring authentic solar system destinations, children repair mid-flight engine failures, harvest planetary resources for fuel, and earn funding to upgrade their rockets. By making critical decisions hands-on, players naturally develop problem-solving skills and a passion for space exploration.

Oyuncular bütçe, kütle, enerji ve yakıt dengesini kurarak kendi uzay araçlarını tasarlıyor. Gerçek gezegenlere iniş yaparak yakıt arıyor, uzaydaki motor arızalarını tamir ediyor ve kazandıkları ödüllerle roketlerini geliştiriyorlar. Bu sayede mühendislik kararlarının sonuçlarını basitçe deneyimleyerek uzay araştırmalarına ve bilime karşı büyük bir merak ve heves kazanıyorlar.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? Our project is an interactive 2D space mission design and survival simulation game that transforms complex aerospace engineering trade-offs into an engaging, hands-on adventure for young learners. The game operates through a three-stage loop:

  1. Hangar & Engineering Design: Players start with a limited budget and select propulsion systems, fuel tanks, power sources, and scientific instruments tailored to their target destination (Moon, Mars, Europa, Titan). Every component dynamically alters the spacecraft's total mass (kg), power draw (Watts), budget ($), and thrust efficiency.
  2. Flight Operations & Crisis Management: During launch and transit, players face real-time space hazards. If micrometeoroids or overheating damage the thruster, players must complete an interactive engineering repair sequence. When fuel runs low, players can land on authentic celestial bodies (such as Asteroid Bennu, Phobos, or Enceladus) to perform ISRU (In-Situ Resource Utilization)—drilling for water ice and methane to refuel their craft.
  3. Evaluation & Progression: Completing mission objectives rewards players with science points and funding, allowing them to upgrade their spacecraft systems and tackle progressively harder deep-space missions.

What are the benefits and intended impact? For most students, concepts like mass-to-fuel ratios, power budgets, and orbital constraints remain abstract textbook theories. Our project makes these trade-offs tangible through learning-by-doing.

  • Benefits: Players intuitively grasp why heavy payloads require stronger rockets, why solar panels lose efficiency near Jupiter, and how resource management determines mission survival.
  • Intended Impact: To demystify STEM and aerospace engineering for children and students, foster critical problem-solving skills, and spark a lifelong curiosity for space exploration.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Software & Languages: Built using 2D game development technologies including HTML5 Canvas, JavaScript, CSS3 / Python / Lua, alongside graphic design and audio editing tools for custom UI, spacecraft sprites, and cinematic intros.
  • NASA Data & Concepts: Referenced NASA open data regarding planetary distances, surface composition, propulsion systems (Ion thrusters, chemical rockets), power generation (Solar arrays vs. MMRTG nuclear systems), and ISRU planetary drilling concepts.
  • Hardware: Developed, compiled, and tested on desktop PC and laptop workstations set up directly at the hackathon venue.

How creative is your project? Traditional mission design tools are often either dry spreadsheet calculators or overwhelmingly complex 3D simulators with steep learning curves. Our creative breakthrough lies in gamifying real NASA engineering trade-offs by blending them with mid-flight survival mechanics—specifically planetary fuel harvesting (ISRU) and interactive module repairs. Players perform real engineering optimization while experiencing the thrill of an arcade space adventure.

What factors did your team consider?

  1. Balancing Realism and Playability: We carefully calibrated the math so that real aerospace constraints drive the gameplay without overwhelming younger players.
  2. Intuitive UI/UX: Instead of walls of numbers, we represented budget, mass, fuel, and power through clear visual gauges and interactive alerts.
  3. Accessibility: We designed a lightweight, standalone experience that runs smoothly across standard school and home computers without requiring high-end hardware.
